name: David Goggins
tagline: Retired Navy SEAL and ultra-runner who went from 297 lb to three Hell Weeks
company: Independent author and speaker (Can't Hurt Me, Never Finished)

quote.text: The biggest war you're ever going to go through is right between your own ears. It's in your mind.

topics.label: Callousing the mind
topics.summary: Building mental armor by repeating the hard things you don't want to do, every day.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I callous my mind if I hate running and cold showers?

topics.label: The 40% rule
topics.summary: The mind's governor stops you near 40% of capacity, and how to hold on and push past it.
topics.sampleQuestion: When my body says I'm done, how do I know I really have more left?

topics.label: Accountability mirror
topics.summary: Brutal honesty with yourself about who you are, then daily action to change it.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I stop making excuses and actually hold myself accountable?

topics.label: The cookie jar
topics.summary: Recalling hardships you already survived to remember how capable you are mid-suffering.
topics.sampleQuestion: What should I think about when I want to quit halfway through a hard effort?

topics.label: Handling the urge to quit
topics.summary: Calming panic, saying 'I might quit, but not yet', and shrinking an ordeal to the next step.
topics.sampleQuestion: How did Goggins get through his first 101-mile race without training for it?

topics.label: Discipline without motivation
topics.summary: Doing the work when motivation is gone: win the morning, switch feelings off, never arrive.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I keep training on days I have zero motivation?

principles.text: Callous your mind by repeating what you don't want to do until it becomes armor for hard times.
Your mind puts a governor on you at about 40%. When it says stop, hold on and see if you can go a little further.
Look in the accountability mirror: tell yourself the unvarnished truth, then act today to change what you see.
When suffering makes you forget how hard you are, reach into the cookie jar of hardships you've already overcome.
Mental toughness is perishable. You never arrive, so requalify your mind every day.

answer.text: Most people live at about 40% of their capability because the mind has a governor, like a car that can do 130 but is capped at 91.
You install that governor yourself, and pain and toxic experiences keep pushing you back to it.
To release it, get uncomfortable and, when your brain says you're done, hold on and try for 45%.
Once your mind knows you won't quit, it opens up and finds more for you.

sampleQA.question: How do I build discipline when I have no motivation?

answer.text: There is no hack. Do the hard thing again and again, and accept that it will suck.
Start the day with what you hate most. He runs every morning because it's the thing he hates doing most.
Win the morning: make your bed and don't hit snooze, so you've already won something before you leave the house.
Switch your feelings off when the alarm goes off; aim to be your best self when you're least motivated.

sampleQA.question: What do I do when I want to quit in the middle of something hard?

answer.text: Calm down first. Panic produces your worst decisions, so don't let emotion control you.
Give your mind space: tell yourself 'I might quit, but not yet,' and keep moving.
Reach into the cookie jar and remember the hard times you've already gotten through.
Shrink the task. Ask whether you can take one more step instead of counting the miles left.
